string-array.name: learn_step_info
string-array.item: We intend to perform ablution and begin by saying “Bismillâhirrahmânirrahîm”.
We wash our hands up to the wrists three times, including between the fingers.
With our right hand, we take water into our mouth, rinse and spit it out three times.
We gently draw water into our nose and clean it three times.
We wash our whole face three times, taking fresh water in our hands each time. Washing the face is an obligatory part of ablution.
Our Prophet (peace be upon him) liked to begin cleaning with the right side. We wash our right arm, including the elbow, three times.
We also wash our left arm, including the elbow, three times. Washing the arms with the elbows is an obligatory part of ablution.
Wiping means passing a wet hand over a surface. Wiping the head is an obligatory part of ablution.
We wipe the inside and back of our ears with wet fingers.
We wipe the back of our neck with the backs of our hands. In the Hanafi school, this is part of the etiquette of ablution. We wash our feet next.
First we wash our right foot, including the ankle, three times and rub between the toes. Washing the feet with the ankles is an obligatory part of ablution.
We also wash our left foot, including the ankle, three times.
After ablution, it is good to say “Eşhedü en lâ ilâhe illallah ve eşhedü enne Muhammeden abdühû ve rasûlüh”.
In prayer we face the Kaaba in Mecca. This direction is called the qibla. We laid out our prayer mat towards it; the tip of its mihrab pattern points towards the qibla.
We intend to perform today\'s obligatory dawn prayer for Allah\'s sake. Actions are judged by intentions.
We raise our hands, say “Allâhu Ekber” and begin prayer. This is called the opening takbir.
We fold our hands while standing and recite the Subhanaka supplication.
We seek refuge in Allah, say the basmala and recite Al-Fatiha. Prayer is not valid without Al-Fatiha.
After Al-Fatiha, we recite a surah or several verses from the Quran. This is the additional recitation.
We say “Allâhu Ekber”, bow, hold our knees and say “Sübhâne rabbiye\'l-azîm” three times.
While rising, we say “Semi\'allâhü limen hamideh”; once upright, we say “Rabbenâ leke\'l-hamd”.
Saying “Allâhu Ekber”, we place our knees, then hands, forehead and nose on the ground. A servant is closest to their Lord in prostration.
In prostration, we say “Sübhâne rabbiye\'l-a\'lâ” three times.
We say “Allâhu Ekber”, rise and sit briefly.
We say “Allâhu Ekber” and prostrate a second time. The Prophet instructed us to prostrate on seven body parts.
Each unit has two prostrations. Now we say “Allâhu Ekber” and stand for the second unit.
In the second unit, we say the basmala, recite Al-Fatiha and then another surah, here Al-Kawthar.
When bowing, we neither raise our head nor let it hang down; we keep our back straight.
We rise from bowing and say “Rabbenâ leke\'l-hamd”, meaning “Our Lord, all praise is Yours”.
We say “Allâhu Ekber” as we lower and raise ourselves.
After sitting briefly, we say “Allâhu Ekber” and prostrate a second time.
We have completed two units. Saying “Allâhu Ekber”, we rise into the final sitting position.
While sitting, we first recite the At-Tahiyyat supplication.
We recite Allahumma salli and Allahumma barik, asking for blessings upon our Prophet.
We recite the Rabbana atina and Rabbanaghfirli supplications.
We turn our head first right, then left and say “Esselâmü aleyküm ve rahmetullah”. Our prayer is complete!

string-array.name: learn_recitation_meanings
string-array.item: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
Intention is made in the heart; it is also good to express it in words.
O Allah, glory and praise be to You. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You.
I seek refuge in Allah from the rejected Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not those who have incurred anger or gone astray.
Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah is the One on whom all depend, while He depends on none. He neither begets nor is born, and none is comparable to Him.
We have surely granted you Al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, it is the one who hates you who is cut off.
Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent. (3 times)
Our Lord, all praise is Yours.
Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. (3 times)

All greetings, worship and good words belong to Allah. O Prophet, may the peace, mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
O Allah, send mercy upon Muhammad and his family as You sent mercy upon Ibrahim and his family. You are indeed worthy of praise, full of glory.
O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family as You blessed Ibrahim and his family. You are indeed worthy of praise, full of glory.
Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, forgive me, my parents and all believers on the Day of Reckoning.
May the peace and mercy of Allah be upon you.
